venues.reason: A Kowloon cha chaan teng shrunk onto Manchester Road, sister to Cheetham Hill's Happy Valley — claypot rice bubbling at the table, and a menu that never once simplifies for the room it's in.

venues.name: Basmati
venues.reason: A working Victorian station house on Pillory Street, trains still audible through dinner — Bangladeshi and Indian cooking that's outlasted the platform it's built on.

venues.name: Underbanks Gallery
venues.reason: Ann-Marie Fowler spotted the empty shop on Little Underbank and filled it herself — new names on the wall most months, and none of the Market Place's queue for the coffee next door.

venues.name: Art Club
venues.reason: A former dress shop on Shaw Road, now easel space by day and a proper drink by night — life drawing on a Tuesday, and nobody minds if you just came for the coffee.

venues.name: Peppery Rose
venues.reason: Aric Leung sold his three Peking Gardens to spend more time at home, then opened this one anyway — pan-Asian plates named for an uncle's old restaurant on the same road.

venues.name: Indian Affair
venues.reason: Blossom Street's second site for Chorlton's own Dilli-style kitchen — the tandoor's the same, the room's just newer.

venues.name: Hooked
venues.reason: Knutsford's own chip shop moved south to a former WA14 unit on Ashley Road — proper batter, and the same fryer standard that built the following in the first place.

venues.name: Nostro Grande
venues.reason: Neapolitan pizza from an oven shipped over from Naples, and a carbonara finished tableside under a whole wheel of Parmesan — the second site for the family behind Hale Road's Nostro Cafe, in the old Frankie & Benny's unit they've made unrecognisable.

venues.name: Buon Cibo
venues.reason: A family-run shopfront on Shaw Road doing stone-baked pizza from a purpose-built oven alongside a proper trattoria menu — carbonara, arrabbiata, and ossobuco that turns up on the board when the mood takes them.

venues.name: Rustik
venues.reason: Burton Road's own Irish-rooted corner, mornings through mid-afternoon only these days — a proper fry-up and coffee in a room that still wears its rustic, session-bar bones.

venues.name: Beer Heroes
venues.reason: Three hundred and fifty bottles under an arched cellar ceiling on Watergate Street, poured or boxed to go — a second room out at Helsby station for the same small operation.

venues.name: Huxley's
venues.reason: Six tables inside, six more out along the City Walls by the Eastgate Clock — Neil and Olga's own microbrewery on tap, in a building they rescued from nothing themselves.

venues.name: Paysan
venues.reason: Rotisserie chicken and frites downstairs on Bridge Street Row, two hundred wines by the glass upstairs in the Cavern of the Curious Gnome — no bookings, and a queue that doesn't seem to mind.

venues.name: Shrub
venues.reason: Plant-based cooking good enough to rank above most of Chester's meat-eating rooms — oyster mushroom skewers on the Rows terrace, and a wine list that never once apologises for the missing dairy.

venues.name: Craft & Company
venues.reason: A 1776 townhouse on Watergate Row rebuilt around gin, craft beer and a stairwell view worth the climb — live music from Thursday, and a speakeasy hush the rest of the week.

Curated by genuine fit to each moment's own character (Date Night: low light, tables for two, worth staying for a third glass; Entertaining a Client: quiet enough to talk, expensive enough to register; Big Group of Friends: rooms that take eight at short notice; Solo Reset: counter seats, unhurried, nobody asking who you're waiting for) — not every venue that could plausibly fit, a curated editorial list same as the original. journeys.title: Date Night in Altrincham
journeys.blurb: A film first so there's something to talk about, then eight minutes on foot to the best pizza in the county.

journeys.title: A Client, Well Handled
journeys.blurb: Height first for the view, then somewhere with tablecloths and a sommelier who knows when to leave you alone.

journeys.title: A Big Northern Quarter Night
journeys.blurb: Nine kitchens to argue over first, then a touring act nobody quite recognised, then last orders somewhere with no sign on the door.

journeys.title: A Slow Ancoats Morning
journeys.blurb: First pour of the day, a free gallery with nobody else in it yet, and viennoiserie to take home.

journeys.title: Dinner, Then Somewhere Quieter
journeys.blurb: A tasting menu that earns the trip out, then a stool at the counter for whoever isn't ready to call it a night.

journeys.title: Ashley Road, Start to Finish
journeys.blurb: A gallery to wander round while everyone's still arriving, then wine, then a table big enough for the whole group.

journeys.title: Sunset Drinks, Caldera Dinner
journeys.blurb: Cocktails on the terrace while the volcano catches the light, then a caldera-side table built on centuries-old recipes.

journeys.title: A Sea-Captain's Table, Then Something Sparkling
journeys.blurb: Dinner inside a restored 1845 mansion, then a glass of Assyrtiko on a veranda too small to feel like a tour stop.

journeys.title: An Afternoon to Yourself in Knutsford
journeys.blurb: Scratch-made brunch alone at the counter, then an hour glazing a plate nobody's waiting on you to finish.

journeys.title: A Day Off the Quad
journeys.blurb: Steam-table eggs at Valois, the Reg's reading rooms for however long the reading takes, then a pint at Jimmy's with nobody checking the time.
